items.s: Dormancy: the state in which a viable propagule fails to germinate although moisture and warmth are adequate. The other options describe Tuber, Bulbil, Germination trigger.

items.q: In this course, Selectivity basis refers to
o: an additive that protects the crop from injury by a compound applied to the same field
the destruction of a compound by soil organisms, the main route of its disappearance
the mechanism, such as differential uptake, translocation or detoxification, that spares the crop
the length of time a compound remains active in the soil after application
items.s: Selectivity basis: the mechanism, such as differential uptake, translocation or detoxification, that spares the crop. The other options describe Safener, Microbial breakdown, Persistence.

items.q: In this course, Stem parasite refers to
o: a species introduced outside its natural range that spreads and displaces native vegetation
the specialised organ through which a parasitic plant taps into the host vascular system
a species that attaches to the aerial parts of its host and draws from its vascular tissue
a species whose entry into a country is forbidden or limited by official phytosanitary regulation
items.s: Stem parasite: a species that attaches to the aerial parts of its host and draws from its vascular tissue. The other options describe Alien invader, Quarantine pest plant, Haustorium.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains Dispersal.
o: the carriage of propagules by wind, helped by plumes, wings or very small size
the movement of propagules away from the parent stand to new ground
the carriage of propagules by flowing water or irrigation current
the capacity of one genotype to vary its form and size with the conditions it meets
items.s: Dispersal: the movement of propagules away from the parent stand to new ground. The other options describe Plasticity, Anemochory, Hydrochory.

items.q: In this course, Pioneer habit refers to
o: the carriage of propagules on animal fur, in hooves or through the gut
the ability to colonise bare, disturbed ground quickly ahead of slower species
the carriage of propagules by flowing water or irrigation current
the capacity of one genotype to vary its form and size with the conditions it meets
items.s: Pioneer habit: the ability to colonise bare, disturbed ground quickly ahead of slower species. The other options describe Zoochory, Hydrochory, Plasticity.

items.q: “application to foliage after the crop and rivals have emerged” is the definition of
o: Post-emergence use
Pre-emergence use
Systemic action
Drift
items.s: Post-emergence use is application to foliage after the crop and rivals have emerged.

items.q: In this course, Leachate refers to
o: the solution of active compounds washed from leaves or litter by rain
a compound released by one plant that suppresses the growth of another
a surface cover of suppressive plant material used to hold back emergence of rivals
material released from living roots into the surrounding soil
items.s: Leachate: the solution of active compounds washed from leaves or litter by rain. The other options describe Allelopathic mulch, Root exudate, Allelochemical.
